posts.title: Hong Kong Radio Show Opportunity for Bangladeshi DJs and Producers
posts.caption:
An incredible opportunity for Bangladeshi Producers and DJ's. 
Send a mix, a bio, a photo and your set goes out from Hong Kong to listeners worldwide, free. 

A radio show gives you what promoters, press and visa applications all look for: proof that your work is heard internationally. That’s the barrier that keeps Bangladeshi artists off stages abroad.

Follow @blu.maron and @subjecttosound and comment 'IN' on their post which is attached below, and they’ll DM you the application link. 
Not a DJ? Share this.

posts.title: Embryonic Shifts: A Stroboscopic STE(A)M Art Installation
posts.caption:
JOIN THE EMBRYONIC SHIFTS — a STE(A)M art installation
Where light, sculpture and science move as one.

We're thrilled to announce Embryonic Shifts, a new stroboscopic sculptural installation by artist Saiqa Shabnam Chowdhury and engineer Samiul Hoque, supported by the British Council under WOW – Women of the World Bangladesh 2025–26.

Using flashing light and the earliest principles of animation, the work makes still sculptures appear to move while telling a story of metamorphosis - a phenomenon every living being goes through in some form or the other.

Taking a clear, empirical stance, the project posits that gender identity is an outcome of biological internal systems rather than an endless social debate. Using persistence of vision—the work examines human perception through empirical science. Fiction and sequential storytelling serve as methods to explore structural realities.
📍 Shala, Aloki
Programme
Opening night — 6:00 pm, Saturday, 22 August 2026 [remarks + introduction to the work]
Exhibition hours — 1:00 PM to 9:00 PM

posts.title: DJ Amit Kirti's DJ Set Inside the Bangladesh Metro Rail
Introverted Film and Erratic Infrastructure: Moving Image in the UK and Bangladesh
posts.caption:
DON'T MISS OUT THIS EXCELLENT SESSION. Registration Info Below:

Delighted to invite 'Introverted Film and Erratic Infrastructure: Histories of Moving Image in the UK and Bangladesh', a lecture and discussion featuring Benjamin Cook (@bwrc00k) in conversation with Dr. Imran Firdaus (@imranfirdaus17) at the British Council Dhaka.

The event forms part of Midnight's Third Child, a year-long research project organised by Benjamin Cook and Kehkasha Sabah, supported through the British Council's Connections Through Culture Grant, with sponsorship from the Durjoy Bangladesh Foundation.

Midnight’s Third Child takes its name from Naeem Mohaiemen’s 2020 book, in which Mohaiemen describes Bangladesh’s cultural identity as occupying a “third space” within the larger postcolonial narratives of South Asia.

We invite you to an illustrated lecture where Benjamin Cook will trace the history of artists’ film in the UK, from the experimental and politically urgent practices of the 1960s and 70s.

In turn, Dr. Imran Firdaus will respond through a parallel genealogy of moving-image practice in Bangladesh—from film societies and cooperative practices to short-film movements, digital video and installation.

Together, they ask:
Where do these histories converge?
Where do they diverge?
What happens to artists’ film when there is no institution built to hold it?

Venue: British Council Auditorium
5 Fuller Road, Dhaka 1000
📅 Sunday, 30 August 2026
⏰ 5–7 PM

RSVP:
Kindly RSVP by Thursday, 29 August 2026

Scan the RSVP QR code or follow the link:
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/gQ5EVQ3T4h?origin=lprLink

posts.title: Rokte Joba: Anime Ontology and Bengali Post-Mysticism
posts.caption:
ARTIST EXPOSURE: @roktejoba @aashnai__ 
attend at https://soloshow.online/symposium_mysticism

rokte joba: anime ontology & bengali post mysticism

for the symposium of post-mysticism at @solo___show (21st-23rd) august, an offsite multimedia showcase and lecture by @aashnai__ 

drawing from her manga practice, she will be sharing the construction of her pictorial world through the theological, iconographic and affective traditions whose social conditions no longer feel inhabitable. on circulating images in the post-liturgical land, enchanted modernities and how the devotional image sustains fractures.

rokte joba is an ongoing image practice and philosophical investigation into the bengali anime ontology.

along with:

jamie sutcliffe + zoe taylor, meltdown your books, elizabeth gabrielle lee, jacob canet-gibson, ojitosdeemoji, nina, yubel, safi, V, nkieve, denpa archivist, knightmaid, yudi wu, vincent, et aliae, saffron-p, carla martin // september: phoenix isla kea, chrysanthi, mirror_doll, archive_doll, evah, sofia, REM, rahul hendriksen, cali constanza, shubi, daniel
